title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). We have a constant base S_0 (probably Spec Z, or a base over Z), a group H, an H-module M (a Z-module, presumably free of finite type, e.g. a lattice), and a group extension 1 -> M -> G -> H -> 1, with G possibly profinite or pro-discrete since the page says 'gr. pro (constants)'. The goal is a group scheme (sheaf of groups) G over S_0 that is an extension of the constant group H_{S_0} by the vector group M ⊗_Z O_S, i.e. M ⊗ G_a. It is obtained by 'linearizing' the kernel M.

The naive definition (30) of the previous page is the pushout extension [G](A) = G ∧_M (M ⊗_Z A), pushed out along M -> M ⊗ A. Its image in H is a single element of H. That is only right when Spec A is connected, because an H_S-valued point should be a locally constant function S -> H.

First construction (this page). Start from the 'incorrect' presheaf [G]: S |-> G ∧_M Γ(S, M ⊗_Z O_S) and take the associated Zariski sheaf. Grothendieck observes that the sheafification is computed by clopen partitions only (formula 33):
  G(S) = colim over partitions S = ∐_{i∈I} U_i into open-and-closed pieces of ∏_i [G](U_i),
the colimit taken over refinement of partitions.

Why this works. A section of the sheaf has a locally constant H-component, so S splits into clopen pieces U_h on which the image is h ∈ H. On U_h the fibre over h is the pushout along M -> M ⊗ O of the M-torsor G_h (the set of lifts of h). That torsor has a point g, so the pushed-out torsor is globally trivial, with section g ∧ 0. Hence local sections with image h glue to an element of [G](U_h). No Čech H^1(M ⊗ O) obstruction appears, because the fibres are trivial torsors.

Second construction. Use the general construction of §49 (an earlier section of this manuscript) in sheaf-theoretic form. The data (34) are:
- an abelian group sheaf M = M ⊗ O_S on S_0;
- the constant pro-group G_{S_0} with distinguished subgroup M_{S_0};
- an operation Θ of G_{S_0} on M, deduced by functoriality from the action of G on M;
- a homomorphism φ: M_{S_0} -> M.
These are subject to compatibility conditions a), b) of §49, presumably: φ is G-equivariant, and Θ restricted to M_{S_0} is conjugation through φ (trivial here, M being abelian).

The construction of loc. cit. then produces (next page) an extension G ⊃ M with φ: G_{S_0} -> G. One recovers (34) from it, φ induces G_{S_0}/M_{S_0} = H_{S_0} ≅ G/M, and so on. This is the standard pushout of a group extension along an equivariant map, G = (M ⋊ G_{S_0}) / {(φ(m)^{-1}, m)}, done in the topos of sheaves on S_0.

Purpose. Within the Longue Marche continuation (Galois–Teichmüller / anabelian material), this attaches to a discrete or profinite extension of H by an abelian M its 'additive' or 'linearized' group-scheme avatar over Z: a two-step, H-relative unipotent-type envelope.
errors: No genuine error. Formula (33) should be read with the U_i open AND closed (an open partition of S is automatically clopen), and for non-quasi-compact S the partitions may be infinite; the product handles this.

The hypothesis H^1(S, M⊗O_S)=0 or S affine, stated on the next page for exactness of G(S) -> H_{S_0}(S) -> 1, is not needed. The fibres are pushouts of trivial M-torsors (G -> H has a set-theoretic section), hence trivial; the marginal note on the next page seems to recognize this ('évidemment triviaux').

ideas.what: Correcting a pushout group functor that fails to be a sheaf on disconnected bases by Zariski sheafification, computed explicitly as a colimit over clopen partitions of products
ideas.modern_name: Sheafification of constant-type presheaves (locally constant functions); the constant group scheme H_S
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (SGA 3 Exp. I / EGA conventions on constant schemes)
ideas.where_published: SGA 3 (constant group schemes, associated sheaves) – general technique

ideas.what: Pushout of a group extension 1->M->G->H->1 along M -> M⊗_Z O_S, giving an extension of the constant group H by the vector group M⊗G_a over Z
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions / first step of relative (unipotent) completion of G relative to H
ideas.usually_credited_to: Pushout of extensions: Eilenberg–MacLane; relative completion: Deligne, Hain (1990s)
ideas.where_published: Not in the published Longue Marche to my knowledge

ideas.what: General construction (§49) building an extension from data (abelian sheaf M, pro-group G with normal subgroup M_0, operation Θ, equivariant φ: M_0 -> M with compatibilities), redone in a sheaf (topos) context
ideas.modern_name: Pushout of extensions along an equivariant map / crossed-module-type data, in a topos
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Schreier, Eilenberg–MacLane); topos version Giraud (Cohomologie non abélienne, 1971)
ideas.where_published: Analogous constructions in SGA 7 Exp. VII and Giraud; the §49 version itself unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck attaches to a (pro-)group extension of H by an abelian M a group scheme over Z that is an extension of the constant group H by the vector group M⊗G_a. In effect this is an integral, length-two, H-relative 'linearized completion' of G, prefiguring relative unipotent/Malcev completion (Deligne, Hain, Hain–Matsumoto), but over Z and with a pro-constant H.
missed.quote: S ⟼ G∧_M Γ(S, M⊗_Z O_S) , et en prenant le faisceau Zariski associé
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral versions of relative completion of profinite/arithmetic fundamental groups are of current interest. This page shows Grothendieck setting up such objects in the Longue Marche continuation, but the construction itself is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Technically correct and careful, but standard: a pushout of extensions plus Zariski sheafification. Its interest lies only in the context, where Grothendieck builds additive group-scheme envelopes of Galois-type group extensions, hinting at relative-completion ideas; nothing here is a new result.
transcription_corrections: '(5)' at top is the page number '(5)' or '(9)'; the archive folio is 18.
'On a une système' should read 'On a un système'.
Label under the first M in (34) likely reads 'Gr. ab. sur S_0' (abelian group sheaf on S_0); under G_{S_0} ⊃ M_{S_0}: 'Gr. pro (constants) sur S_0, M_{S_0} distingué'; then 'homo φ : M_{S_0} → M'.
'au dernier satisfaisant aux conditions' is more plausibly 'ces données satisfaisant aux conditions de compatibilité a) b) de loc. cit.'
In the parenthesis: 'qui revient à une op. de G sur M, est celle déduite de l'op. de G sur M, par fonctorialité' – the second M is the plain Z-module M, the first the sheaf M (underlined).
'(U_i)_{i∈I} une partition de S en ouverts' – the line below reads 'i.e. S ≃ ∐ U_i'.
